# RFC-0006: NSys source wire contract

> **Version:** 0.2.1 | **Status:** normative | **Phase:** stable

**References:** [RFC-0001](../rfc/RFC-0001.md), [RFC-0002](../rfc/RFC-0002.md), [RFC-0003](../rfc/RFC-0003.md), [RFC-0004](../rfc/RFC-0004.md), [RFC-0005](../rfc/RFC-0005.md), [RFC-0002:C-DEFAULT-MACHINE-OUTPUT](../rfc/RFC-0002.md#rfc-0002c-default-machine-output), [RFC-0002:C-SUCCESS-RESPONSE](../rfc/RFC-0002.md#rfc-0002c-success-response), [RFC-0002:C-ERROR-RESPONSE](../rfc/RFC-0002.md#rfc-0002c-error-response), [RFC-0002:C-STDOUT-STDERR](../rfc/RFC-0002.md#rfc-0002c-stdout-stderr), [RFC-0002:C-FORMAT-PROJECTIONS](../rfc/RFC-0002.md#rfc-0002c-format-projections), [RFC-0002:C-EXCEPTIONS](../rfc/RFC-0002.md#rfc-0002c-exceptions), [RFC-0003:C-ROW-KEY](../rfc/RFC-0003.md#rfc-0003c-row-key), [RFC-0004:C-SOURCE-IDENTITY](../rfc/RFC-0004.md#rfc-0004c-source-identity), [RFC-0004:C-SOURCE-VERSION](../rfc/RFC-0004.md#rfc-0004c-source-version), [RFC-0004:C-TRACE-DETECTION](../rfc/RFC-0004.md#rfc-0004c-trace-detection), [RFC-0004:C-COMMAND-SURFACE](../rfc/RFC-0004.md#rfc-0004c-command-surface), [RFC-0004:C-SOURCE-EXCEPTIONS](../rfc/RFC-0004.md#rfc-0004c-source-exceptions), [RFC-0005:C-ARTIFACT-ROOT](../rfc/RFC-0005.md#rfc-0005c-artifact-root), [RFC-0005:C-FRESHNESS](../rfc/RFC-0005.md#rfc-0005c-freshness), [RFC-0003:C-LIST-SHAPE](../rfc/RFC-0003.md#rfc-0003c-list-shape), [RFC-0003:C-AUXILIARY-DATA](../rfc/RFC-0003.md#rfc-0003c-auxiliary-data)

---

## 1. Summary

### [RFC-0006:C-SUMMARY] Summary (Informative) <a id="rfc-0006c-summary"></a>

This RFC specifies the Nsight Systems source wire contract for VeloQ.
It refines the product, CLI I/O, list identity, source, and artifact contracts in [RFC-0001](../rfc/RFC-0001.md), [RFC-0002](../rfc/RFC-0002.md), [RFC-0003](../rfc/RFC-0003.md), [RFC-0004](../rfc/RFC-0004.md), and [RFC-0005](../rfc/RFC-0005.md).

**Scope:** This RFC covers the stable NSys source identity, supported input forms, source-owned command IDs, NSys event row identifiers, EventRef objects, concrete NSys row key formats, NVTX identity semantics, generated artifact readiness reporting, and source-specific stdout exceptions. It does not prescribe SQL architecture, query helper layout, private cache record schemas, DuckDB table names, Parquet sidecar schemas, implementation module names, or gated unstable response shapes.

**Rationale:** NSys is the default and broadest VeloQ source. Agents need stable source-specific row identities, event references, and cache-readiness evidence so they can compare traces, inspect rows, correlate CPU/GPU evidence, and decide whether a profile is prepared without reverse-engineering private query implementation.

_Since: v0.1.0_

---

## 2. Specification

### [RFC-0006:C-SOURCE-IDENTITY] Source identity (Normative) <a id="rfc-0006c-source-identity"></a>

NSys success responses MUST set `source.kind` to `nsys`.

NSys success responses MUST set `source.version` to `v2` for the wire contract specified by this RFC version.

NSys handled error responses MUST set `source.kind` to `nsys` when source context is known and no explicit raw-output exception applies.

NSys handled error responses MUST set `source.version` to `v2` when source context is known and no explicit raw-output exception applies.

The NSys source namespace MUST be `nsys`.

A breaking change to an NSys source payload MUST change the NSys source version according to [RFC-0004:C-SOURCE-VERSION](../rfc/RFC-0004.md#rfc-0004c-source-version).

An NSys source-owned command ID MUST use the `nsys.<verb>` form.

An NSys command invoked through a default-source hoisted alias MUST preserve the same `nsys.<verb>` command ID in the envelope.

An NSys trace-bearing success response MUST include `trace` when the input path is known.

An NSys trace-bearing handled error response MUST include `trace` when the input path is known and no explicit raw-output exception applies.

An NSys response with `trace_span` MUST set `trace_span.origin_ns` to an integer nanosecond origin.

An NSys response with `trace_span` MUST set `trace_span.span_ns` to an integer nanosecond duration.

The NSys `schema` command MUST NOT require a trace input.

The NSys `schema` command MUST omit `trace` and `trace_span` from its envelope.

Source version `v1` was the initial stable NSys wire contract.

Source version `v2` supersedes `v1` by changing NSys `prep` and `prep --status` to the canonical list response defined by [RFC-0006:C-ARTIFACTS](../rfc/RFC-0006.md#rfc-0006c-artifacts).

**Rationale:** Source identity, source version, and command IDs are the dispatch context agents use after parsing an envelope. Hoisted aliases are a CLI convenience; they must not create a second wire identity for the same source command. Version `v2` marks the breaking cleanup that makes NSys `prep` and `prep --status` sidecar-readiness lists instead of singleton cache summaries.

_Since: v0.1.0_

### [RFC-0006:C-SUPPORTED-INPUTS] Supported inputs (Normative) <a id="rfc-0006c-supported-inputs"></a>

NSys automatic source detection MUST follow the side-effect-free trace detection contract in [RFC-0004:C-TRACE-DETECTION](../rfc/RFC-0004.md#rfc-0004c-trace-detection).

NSys automatic source detection MUST claim `.nsys-rep` inputs.

NSys automatic source detection MUST claim direct `_pqtdir` directory inputs.

NSys automatic source detection MAY claim a generated `parquetdir/` child only when that path can be resolved as an alias for the owning `.nsys-rep` artifact root specified by [RFC-0005:C-ARTIFACT-ROOT](../rfc/RFC-0005.md#rfc-0005c-artifact-root).

NSys automatic source detection MUST NOT claim `.sqlite` inputs.

An NSys trace-bearing command MUST emit a handled diagnostic error when the supplied input is not a supported NSys input and no explicit raw-output exception applies.

An NSys command that opens a supported input MUST keep generated artifacts under the artifact root defined by [RFC-0005:C-ARTIFACT-ROOT](../rfc/RFC-0005.md#rfc-0005c-artifact-root).

**Rationale:** Agents need source detection to be deterministic and side-effect-free. Alias handling keeps generated `parquetdir/` paths usable without splitting cache ownership across multiple artifact roots.

_Since: v0.1.0_

### [RFC-0006:C-COMMAND-SURFACE] Command surface (Normative) <a id="rfc-0006c-command-surface"></a>

The stable NSys source-owned command surface MUST include `summary`, `stats`, `search`, `inspect`, `correlate`, `gaps`, `slices`, `timeline`, `concurrency`, `graph-replays`, `hardware`, `metrics`, `prep`, `correlation-stats`, `ncu-command`, and `schema`.

The stable NSys source-owned command surface MUST preserve the source command rules in [RFC-0004:C-COMMAND-SURFACE](../rfc/RFC-0004.md#rfc-0004c-command-surface).

A gated hidden or unstable NSys command or schema target MUST NOT be treated as part of the stable public command surface until this clause explicitly lists it as stable.

A gated hidden or unstable NSys response shape MUST NOT be covered by the stable compatibility guarantees in this RFC.

The `schema` command MUST emit a normal VeloQ JSON envelope.

The `schema` command envelope `data` field MUST contain the requested JSON schema document.

The `schema` command MUST omit `trace` because it does not inspect a trace.

A command added to the stable NSys public command surface MUST either conform to the contracts in [RFC-0002](../rfc/RFC-0002.md), [RFC-0003](../rfc/RFC-0003.md), and this RFC, or document a source-specific exception in this RFC.

**Rationale:** The command surface is part of the external agent contract. Gated development surfaces can exist without accidentally becoming stable wire contracts.

_Since: v0.1.0_

### [RFC-0006:C-ROW-ID] Event row identifiers (Normative) <a id="rfc-0006c-row-id"></a>

An NSys event identifier exposed as `row_id` MUST use the `<kind>:<rowid>` string form.

The `<kind>` component MUST be one of `kernel`, `memcpy`, `memset`, `runtime`, `osrt`, `nvtx`, `sync`, `graph`, `graph_node`, `graph_event`, `cuda_event`, `overhead`, or `cpu_sample`.

The `<rowid>` component MUST be a base-10 integer string.

The `<rowid>` component MUST be compatible with the source row identifier accepted by NSys `inspect`.

An NSys `row_id` MUST be round-trippable through `inspect`.

The `cpu_sample` row identifier kind MAY appear in inspect-compatible identifiers.

The `cpu_sample` row identifier kind MUST NOT appear as an EventRef `type` value.

An NSys `inspect` request for a syntactically valid but absent `row_id` MUST return a success response.

An NSys `inspect` response for an absent `row_id` MUST include a row tagged with `type: "not_found"`.

An NSys `inspect` not-found row MUST carry `key` equal to the requested `row_id`.

An NSys `inspect` not-found row MUST carry `row_id` equal to the requested `row_id`.

An NSys `row_id` MUST NOT expose a packed binary correlation key in place of the human-readable `<kind>:<rowid>` form.

A packed synthetic identifier MAY appear only in a field whose contract explicitly defines a synthetic identifier.

**Rationale:** Agents commonly take a search or correlate row and pass its `row_id` to inspect. Keeping the wire identifier readable and round-trippable separates user-facing identity from private indexing strategies. CPU samples are inspect evidence, not duration-bearing EventRef rows.

_Since: v0.1.0_

### [RFC-0006:C-EVENT-REF] EventRef objects (Normative) <a id="rfc-0006c-event-ref"></a>

Each row in `search.rows[]` MUST be an EventRef object.

Each embedded event in `correlate.rows[].events[]` MUST be an EventRef object.

An EventRef object MUST carry a top-level `type` discriminator.

The EventRef `type` value MUST be one of `kernel`, `memcpy`, `memset`, `sync`, `runtime`, `osrt`, `nvtx`, `graph`, `graph_node`, `graph_event`, `cuda_event`, or `overhead`.

An EventRef object MUST carry `key`, `row_id`, `name`, `start_ns`, and `duration_ns`.

An EventRef `key` MUST be a string.

An EventRef `row_id` MUST follow [RFC-0006:C-ROW-ID](../rfc/RFC-0006.md#rfc-0006c-row-id).

An EventRef `name` MUST be a string.

An EventRef `start_ns` MUST be an integer nanosecond timestamp in the opened trace timebase.

An EventRef `duration_ns` MUST be an integer nanosecond duration.

An EventRef object MAY carry `device_id`, `stream_id`, `global_tid`, `depth`, and `nvtx_context` when those values are known for the event.

An EventRef `device_id`, `stream_id`, and `global_tid` value MUST be an integer when present.

An EventRef `depth` value MUST be a non-negative integer when present.

A `kernel` EventRef SHOULD carry `grid`, `block`, `registers_per_thread`, `static_shared_memory`, `dynamic_shared_memory`, `demangled_name`, and `mangled_name` when those values are available in the trace.

A `kernel` EventRef `grid` value MUST be an array of three integers when present.

A `kernel` EventRef `block` value MUST be an array of three integers when present.

A `kernel` EventRef `registers_per_thread`, `static_shared_memory`, and `dynamic_shared_memory` value MUST be an integer when present.

A `kernel` EventRef `demangled_name` and `mangled_name` value MUST be a string when present.

A `memcpy` EventRef SHOULD carry `bytes`, `copy_kind`, and `copy_kind_name` when those values are available in the trace.

A `memcpy` EventRef `bytes` value MUST be an integer byte count when present.

A `memcpy` EventRef `copy_kind` value MUST be an integer when present.

A `memcpy` EventRef `copy_kind_name` value MUST be a string when present.

A `memset` EventRef SHOULD carry `bytes` and `value` when those values are available in the trace.

A `memset` EventRef `bytes` value MUST be an integer byte count when present.

A `memset` EventRef `value` value MUST be an integer when present.

An `nvtx` EventRef SHOULD carry `event_type` and `domain_id` when those values are available in the trace.

An `nvtx` EventRef `event_type` and `domain_id` value MUST be an integer when present.

An EventRef MUST omit unavailable optional values instead of fabricating placeholder values.

An EventRef `key` MUST equal its `row_id` unless a future source version explicitly defines a different key contract.

**Rationale:** EventRef is the shared row shape that lets agents inspect search and correlation evidence without an immediate follow-up query for common headline fields. Optional values reflect trace schema variation; fabricated values would make agent conclusions less trustworthy.

_Since: v0.1.0_

### [RFC-0006:C-ROW-KEYS] Concrete row keys (Normative) <a id="rfc-0006c-row-keys"></a>

An NSys row key defined by this clause MUST be treated as an opaque equality string by consumers.

An NSys row key consumer MUST NOT require delimiter-based parsing of a row key.

An NSys row key producer MUST preserve the key formats in this clause for stable public responses.

Optional pipe-delimited segments in the row key templates below are shown with square brackets.

A bracketed optional segment MUST be omitted when that identity axis is absent.

The square brackets MUST NOT appear literally in a row key.

A sentinel value such as `nvtx:none` or `nvtx-path:none` is a present segment, not an absent axis.

Trace-derived key components MAY contain delimiter characters.

An NSys `summary` row key MUST use `table|<table_name>`.

An NSys `stats` row key MUST use `<kind>[|<name>][|dev:<n>][|stream:<n>][|ctx:<n>][|graph:<n>][|graph_node:<n>][|style:<push_pop|start_end|unknown>][|nvtx:<rowid-or-none>][|nvtx-path:<path-or-none>][|domain:<pid>:<domainId>][|grid:<x>x<y>x<z>][|block:<x>x<y>x<z>]`.

An NSys `stats` row key for a no-NVTX parent sentinel MUST use `nvtx:none` for the NVTX parent segment.

An NSys `stats` row key for a no-NVTX path sentinel MUST use `nvtx-path:none` for the NVTX path segment.

An NSys `stats` row key for a real NVTX path row MUST include `domain:<pid>:<domainId>`.

An NSys `search` row key MUST use `<row_id>`.

An NSys `inspect` row key MUST use `<row_id>`.

An NSys `inspect` not-found row key MUST use the requested `<row_id>`.

An NSys `timeline` row key MUST use `bucket|<start_ns>..<end_ns>`.

An NSys `concurrency` row key MUST use `concurrency|dev:<n>`.

An NSys `slices` instance row key MUST use `slice|<name>|@<cpu_start_ns>`.

An NSys `slices` aggregate row key MUST use `scope|<name>` or `scope|path:<path>` according to the requested grouping mode.

An NSys device-scope `gaps` row key MUST use `gap|dev:<n>|@<start_ns>`.

An NSys stream-scope `gaps` row key MUST use `gap|dev:<n>|stream:<n>|@<start_ns>`.

An NSys trace-scope `gaps` row key MUST use `gap|@<start_ns>`.

An NSys `gaps.auxiliary.streams[]` row key MUST use `stream|dev:<n>|stream:<n>`.

An NSys `prep` row key MUST use `sidecar|<sidecar-id>`.

An NSys `correlate` result row key MUST use the seed row identifier.

An EventRef embedded under an NSys `correlate` result MUST use `<row_id>` as its key.

An NSys `graph-replays` row key MUST use `graph-replay|<synthetic_id>`.

An NSys `hardware` row key MUST use `host|<hostname>`.

An NSys GPU `metrics.rows[]` row key MUST use `counter|type:<type_id>|metric:<metric_id>`.

An NSys GPU `metrics.auxiliary.buckets[]` row key MUST use `bucket|<t_start_ns>|type:<type_id>|metric:<metric_id>`.

An NSys NIC `metrics.rows[]` row key MUST use `nic_counter|nic:<id>|port:<id>|metric:<idx>`.

An NSys NIC `metrics.auxiliary.buckets[]` row key MUST use `nic_bucket|<t_start_ns>|nic:<id>|port:<id>|metric:<idx>`.

An NSys CPU sampling `metrics.rows[]` row key MUST use the selected grouping identity: bare `<symbol>`, `<module-basename>`, `<tid>`, `<cpu>`, or `stack|<stack_hash>`.

An NSys CPU sampling `metrics.auxiliary.cpu_buckets[]` row key MUST use the selected non-stack grouping identity: bare `<symbol>`, `<module-basename>`, `<tid>`, or `<cpu>`.

An NSys CPU scheduler `metrics.rows[]` row key MUST use the selected grouping identity: `tid:<id>`, `cpu:<id>`, or `state:<name>`.

An NSys CPU scheduler `metrics.auxiliary.cpu_buckets[]` row key MUST use the selected grouping identity: `tid:<id>`, `cpu:<id>`, or `state:<name>`.

A command that emits a canonical NSys list row and is not listed in this clause MUST define its row key format before the command is advanced as a stable public surface.

A command that emits a stable NSys auxiliary list whose rows carry `key` MUST define that auxiliary row key format before the command or mode is advanced as a stable public surface.

**Rationale:** [RFC-0003:C-ROW-KEY](../rfc/RFC-0003.md#rfc-0003c-row-key) requires comparable rows to carry stable keys but intentionally leaves concrete formats to source and verb contracts. These NSys formats are equality keys for cross-trace comparison, not a general key-parsing language. `prep` sidecar rows are included because agents use them to compare cache readiness across repeated trace-analysis sessions. Metrics bucket arrays are documented here because they are stable auxiliary lists used for time-series comparison.

_Since: v0.1.0_

### [RFC-0006:C-NVTX-IDENTITY] NVTX identity (Normative) <a id="rfc-0006c-nvtx-identity"></a>

NSys `stats --group-by nvtx-path` rows for real NVTX ranges MUST include the NVTX domain dimension in row identity.

NSys `stats --group-by nvtx-path` row keys for real NVTX ranges MUST include the `domain:<pid>:<domainId>` segment defined by [RFC-0006:C-ROW-KEYS](../rfc/RFC-0006.md#rfc-0006c-row-keys).

NSys `stats --group-by nvtx-path` rows for real NVTX ranges MUST expose resolved `domain_id` and `domain_pid` values when the trace provides them.

NSys `stats --group-by nvtx-path` rows MAY expose `domain_name` when the trace provides a registered domain name.

Same-name and same-parent NVTX ranges in distinct domains MUST remain distinct rows when the requested grouping includes the NVTX path axis.

A sentinel or no-NVTX row MUST NOT fabricate a domain identity.

A row key that includes the NVTX style axis MUST use one of `push_pop`, `start_end`, or `unknown` for the style value.

A command that requires `NVTX_EVENTS` MUST return a handled diagnostic error when the opened trace lacks `NVTX_EVENTS` and no explicit raw-output exception applies.

A command that can answer without `NVTX_EVENTS` MUST NOT fail solely because `NVTX_EVENTS` is absent.

**Rationale:** NVTX labels are often reused across domains and processes. Domain-aware identity prevents false joins, while explicit missing-table behavior keeps optional NSys schema features from becoming accidental global requirements.

_Since: v0.1.0_

### [RFC-0006:C-SOURCE-EXCEPTIONS] Source-specific output exceptions (Normative) <a id="rfc-0006c-source-exceptions"></a>

`ncu-command --print` MAY write a raw pipe-ready command script to stdout instead of a JSON success envelope.

`ncu-command --print` MUST keep stdout reserved for the raw script when it succeeds.

`ncu-command --print` MUST NOT mix progress output with the raw script on stdout.

`ncu-command --print` MUST NOT write a partial raw script to stdout when it fails.

`ncu-command --print` MUST NOT write a JSON error envelope to stdout when it fails.

`ncu-command --print` MUST write a human-readable failure diagnostic to stderr when it fails.

`ncu-command --print` MUST return a non-zero process status when it fails.

`ncu-command` without `--print` MUST use the normal JSON envelope contract.

NSys `metrics --bucket` MAY return its time-series rows under the source-specific auxiliary bucket list instead of `data.rows[]`.

NSys GPU and NIC `metrics --bucket` responses MUST place bucket rows under `data.auxiliary.buckets[]`.

NSys CPU sampling and CPU scheduler `metrics --bucket` responses MUST place bucket rows under `data.auxiliary.cpu_buckets[]`.

NSys `metrics --bucket` responses MUST leave `data.rows[]` empty.

NSys `metrics --bucket` response `count` MUST equal the number of returned bucket rows in the active auxiliary bucket list.

NSys `metrics --bucket` response `total_matched` MUST equal the number of matching bucket rows before response limiting.

NSys `metrics --bucket` auxiliary bucket rows MUST carry row keys defined by [RFC-0006:C-ROW-KEYS](../rfc/RFC-0006.md#rfc-0006c-row-keys).

NSys metrics responses without `--bucket` MUST use normal canonical `data.rows[]` list semantics.

NSys JSON-mode handled diagnostics MUST follow [RFC-0002:C-ERROR-RESPONSE](../rfc/RFC-0002.md#rfc-0002c-error-response) and [RFC-0002:C-STDOUT-STDERR](../rfc/RFC-0002.md#rfc-0002c-stdout-stderr).

NSys CSV and table outputs MUST follow [RFC-0002:C-FORMAT-PROJECTIONS](../rfc/RFC-0002.md#rfc-0002c-format-projections).

**Rationale:** `ncu-command --print` is designed to be piped directly into a shell or saved by a caller, so its raw stdout behavior is intentional. Metrics bucket mode is a source-specific time-series projection whose bucket rows have source-dependent shapes that differ from the summary rows in `data.rows[]`; documenting the exception preserves current agent-readable behavior while making its pagination and key semantics explicit. Other NSys commands remain envelope-shaped for agent parsing.

_Since: v0.1.0_

### [RFC-0006:C-COMPATIBILITY] Compatibility (Normative) <a id="rfc-0006c-compatibility"></a>

Adding optional fields to an NSys response MAY keep source version `v2` when existing documented fields, row keys, command IDs, and output-mode semantics remain compatible.

Removing an NSys response field documented by this RFC MUST change the NSys source version according to [RFC-0004:C-SOURCE-VERSION](../rfc/RFC-0004.md#rfc-0004c-source-version).

Changing the type or meaning of an NSys response field documented by this RFC MUST change the NSys source version.

Changing an NSys row key format defined by [RFC-0006:C-ROW-KEYS](../rfc/RFC-0006.md#rfc-0006c-row-keys) MUST change the NSys source version.

Changing an NSys auxiliary bucket row key format defined by [RFC-0006:C-ROW-KEYS](../rfc/RFC-0006.md#rfc-0006c-row-keys) MUST change the NSys source version.

Changing the `row_id` format defined by [RFC-0006:C-ROW-ID](../rfc/RFC-0006.md#rfc-0006c-row-id) MUST change the NSys source version.

Changing the EventRef `type` discriminator contract defined by [RFC-0006:C-EVENT-REF](../rfc/RFC-0006.md#rfc-0006c-event-ref) MUST change the NSys source version.

Changing the `source.kind` value from `nsys` MUST be treated as a breaking source identity change under [RFC-0004:C-SOURCE-IDENTITY](../rfc/RFC-0004.md#rfc-0004c-source-identity).

Changing a stable NSys command ID MUST be treated as a breaking command-surface change under [RFC-0004:C-COMMAND-SURFACE](../rfc/RFC-0004.md#rfc-0004c-command-surface).

Removing support for a supported NSys input form defined by [RFC-0006:C-SUPPORTED-INPUTS](../rfc/RFC-0006.md#rfc-0006c-supported-inputs) MUST be treated as a breaking trace-detection change under [RFC-0004:C-TRACE-DETECTION](../rfc/RFC-0004.md#rfc-0004c-trace-detection).

Changing the `ncu-command --print` raw-output exception defined by [RFC-0006:C-SOURCE-EXCEPTIONS](../rfc/RFC-0006.md#rfc-0006c-source-exceptions) MUST be treated as a breaking output exception change unless the change is strictly additive for raw-output consumers.

Changing the `metrics --bucket` list-shape exception defined by [RFC-0006:C-SOURCE-EXCEPTIONS](../rfc/RFC-0006.md#rfc-0006c-source-exceptions) MUST be treated as a breaking output exception change unless the change is strictly additive for bucket-mode consumers.

Changing the NSys `prep` canonical list shape defined by [RFC-0006:C-ARTIFACTS](../rfc/RFC-0006.md#rfc-0006c-artifacts) MUST change the NSys source version.

The NSys source version `v2` envelope shape MUST remain compatible with [RFC-0002:C-SUCCESS-RESPONSE](../rfc/RFC-0002.md#rfc-0002c-success-response) and [RFC-0002:C-ERROR-RESPONSE](../rfc/RFC-0002.md#rfc-0002c-error-response).

The NSys source version `v2` list rows MUST remain compatible with [RFC-0003:C-ROW-KEY](../rfc/RFC-0003.md#rfc-0003c-row-key).

The NSys source version `v2` artifact ownership semantics MUST remain compatible with [RFC-0005:C-ARTIFACT-ROOT](../rfc/RFC-0005.md#rfc-0005c-artifact-root) and [RFC-0005:C-FRESHNESS](../rfc/RFC-0005.md#rfc-0005c-freshness).

The NSys source version `v2` supersedes source version `v1` by changing `prep` and `prep --status` from singleton cache summaries to the canonical sidecar-readiness list defined by [RFC-0006:C-ARTIFACTS](../rfc/RFC-0006.md#rfc-0006c-artifacts).

**Rationale:** Source-specific compatibility rules make it clear which NSys changes are additive and which changes require a source-version bump so agents can trust stored parsing logic. The `v2` bump keeps the cache-readiness cleanup explicit instead of preserving older singleton `prep` fields through compatibility wrappers.

_Since: v0.1.0_

### [RFC-0006:C-ARTIFACTS] Artifacts and prep readiness (Normative) <a id="rfc-0006c-artifacts"></a>

NSys generated artifacts MUST live under the VeloQ artifact root for the resolved NSys source path according to [RFC-0005:C-ARTIFACT-ROOT](../rfc/RFC-0005.md#rfc-0005c-artifact-root).

An NSys command that accepts a generated `parquetdir/` alias MUST resolve generated artifacts under the owning `.nsys-rep` artifact root.

The registered NSys sidecar inventory for source version `v2` MUST include `meta-cache` and `gpu-work-events`.

A registered NSys sidecar id MUST be a stable lowercase ASCII identifier.

The `meta-cache` sidecar id MUST refer to the VeloQ metadata cache file named `meta.bin`.

The `gpu-work-events` sidecar id MUST refer to the normalized GPU work interval sidecar file named `gpu-work-events.parquet`.

NSys `prep` without `--status` MUST prepare every registered NSys sidecar before emitting its response.

NSys `prep --status` MUST report registered NSys sidecar state without creating, rewriting, or refreshing any registered sidecar file.

NSys `prep` and `prep --status` MUST emit the same canonical list response shape defined by [RFC-0003:C-LIST-SHAPE](../rfc/RFC-0003.md#rfc-0003c-list-shape).

NSys `prep` response `data.rows[]` MUST report one row per registered NSys sidecar id in source version `v2`.

Each NSys `prep` response `data.rows[]` row `key` MUST be a string using the `sidecar|<sidecar-id>` format defined by [RFC-0006:C-ROW-KEYS](../rfc/RFC-0006.md#rfc-0006c-row-keys).

Each NSys `prep` response `data.rows[]` row `name` MUST be the sidecar filename as a string.

Each NSys `prep` response `data.rows[]` row `path` MUST be the filesystem path where that sidecar is expected under the owning artifact root.

Each NSys `prep` response `data.rows[]` row `present` MUST be a boolean that is `true` when a filesystem entry exists at `path`.

Each NSys `prep` response `data.rows[]` row `format_version_expected` MUST be an integer sidecar schema version expected by the current VeloQ binary.

Each NSys `prep` response `data.rows[]` row `format_version_on_disk` MUST be an integer sidecar schema version when a readable sidecar version is present on disk.

Each NSys `prep` response `data.rows[]` row MUST omit `format_version_on_disk` when the sidecar is absent, unreadable, or does not expose a readable sidecar version.

Each NSys `prep` response `data.rows[]` row `fingerprint_match` MUST be a boolean that is `true` only when VeloQ can prove that the sidecar is fresh for the resolved source evidence and expected sidecar version.

Each NSys `prep` response `data.rows[]` row `fingerprint_match` MUST be `false` for absent, stale, unreadable, wrong-version, or unversioned sidecars.

NSys `prep` response `data.auxiliary.cache_root` MUST be the artifact root path string for the resolved source path.

NSys `prep` response `data.auxiliary.parquet_cache` MUST describe the NSys parquet export used as the raw-table cache.

NSys `prep` response `data.auxiliary.parquet_cache.dir` MUST be the parquetdir path string.

NSys `prep` response `data.auxiliary.parquet_cache.present` MUST be a boolean that is `true` when the parquetdir exists.

NSys `prep` response `data.auxiliary.parquet_cache.tables` MUST be a sorted string array of present parquet table stems.

NSys `prep` response `data.auxiliary.prepared` MUST be a boolean that reports whether this command invocation performed preparation.

NSys `prep` response `data.auxiliary.prepared` MUST be `true` for `prep` without `--status`.

NSys `prep` response `data.auxiliary.prepared` MUST be `false` for `prep --status`.

NSys `prep` response `data.auxiliary.elapsed_ms` MUST be an integer elapsed time in milliseconds for the `prep` or `prep --status` command invocation.

NSys query commands MUST NOT require callers to know private sidecar file formats or private sidecar schemas.

Optional NSys acceleration sidecars MUST NOT make unrelated commands fail when the command can preserve public evidence semantics without using that sidecar.

**Rationale:** `prep` is how agents ask whether a trace is ready for repeated analysis. A canonical sidecar list makes readiness machine-joinable, avoids ad hoc singleton cache fields, and keeps optional acceleration artifacts from becoming hidden global dependencies. The sidecar inventory and field semantics are explicit so tests can verify row completeness, key stability, and missing/stale sidecar behavior without depending on private record schemas.

_Since: v0.2.1_
